answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a per-agent cost bond anchored in verified unique work. A joining agent must submit a hardware-attested quote keyed to an unclonable quartz oscillator's jitter, then solve a cipher puzzle bound to that key. The resulting thread of signed micro-tasks is publicly auditable and cannot be transferred, so every extra identity must re-pay the bond and redo fresh work. A farm of a thousand sock puppets therefore costs a thousand times one honest agent's marginal expense.
